intro.title: Business Planning
paragraphs: Welcome to the Business Planning Workshop! You have just entered a conference room where everything has been prepared for a hands-on session about building a Business Model Canvas.

The room contains several interactive stations - a fogged window, a flip chart, a wall-mounted TV, papers on the table, and a folder. Each station holds a puzzle that will teach you a key component of the Business Model Canvas.
Complete all five puzzles in any order you like. Once all are done, the whiteboard at the front will light up to reveal your completed Business Model Canvas. Good luck!

customerSegments.title: Customer Segments
customerSegments.instructions: Classify each customer segment as Valid or Invalid. Valid segments are specific and actionable. Invalid segments are too broad, vague, or assumption-based.

customers.0: Freelancers and remote workers who value flexible services
customers.1: Parents of young children who prioritize safety
customers.3: Everyone who has ever needed something
customers.4: Office workers who need quick solutions during the workday
customers.6: Retirees who value personal customer service
customers.7: Small business owners who want to save time
customers.8: People who will definitely love the business
customers.9: People who accidentally clicked the website link
customers.10: People who juggle several tasks during the workday, and need efficient tools

invalidExplanations.3: Too broad - this describes virtually everyone and is not a useful segment.
invalidExplanations.5: Too vague - 'nice things' does not define a specific need or behavior.
invalidExplanations.8: Assumption-based - you cannot assume people will love your business.
invalidExplanations.9: Not actual customers - accidental clicks do not represent real interest.

feedback.wrong: Not quite. Think about whether this segment is specific and actionable.
feedback.allCorrect: Excellent! You have correctly classified all customer segments!

customerSegments.answerOverlay:
Valid segments: Freelancers and remote workers, Parents of young children, Students looking for cost-saving options, Office workers who need quick solutions, Retirees who value personal customer service, Small business owners who want to save time, People who juggle several tasks.

Invalid segments: 'Everyone who has ever needed something' (too broad), 'People who like nice things' (too vague), 'People who will definitely love the business' (assumption-based), 'People who accidentally clicked the website link' (not actual customers).

valueProposition.title: Value Proposition
valueProposition.instructions: This value proposition contains unnecessary buzzwords. Click on the parts that should be REMOVED (struck through). Keep only the meaningful parts, then submit.

parts.1: solutions that help people save time
parts.3: by reducing unnecessary steps in everyday tasks

feedback.wrong: Some parts are not correctly marked. Remember: keep what is meaningful and specific, remove buzzwords and filler.
feedback.hint: Hint: Keep only the parts that describe a concrete benefit or action. Remove corporate jargon.
feedback.correct: Perfect! You stripped away the buzzwords and kept the clear value proposition.

valueProposition.answerOverlay:
Keep: 'solutions that help people save time' and 'by reducing unnecessary steps in everyday tasks'.

Remove: 'We offer innovative', 'world-class quality', 'through excellence', 'and cutting-edge synergy', 'using next-generation features'.

channels.title: Channels
channels.introText: Match each customer behavior with the most appropriate channel to reach them. Use the arrows to scroll through available channels, then confirm your selection.

behaviors.0: Customers who are active online and engage with social platforms
behaviors.1: Customers who rely on recommendations from friends and family
behaviors.2: Customers who are looking for services during work hours nearby
behaviors.3: Customers who prefer direct personal contact for inquiries

channelOptions: Direct Contact via Email or Phone

feedback.wrong: That channel does not match this customer behavior. Try another.
feedback.allCorrect: Great job! You matched all customer behaviors to their ideal channels!

channels.answerOverlay:
Correct matches:
1. Active online/social platforms -> Social Media
2. Rely on recommendations -> Word of Mouth
3. Looking for services during work hours -> Physical Location
4. Prefer direct personal contact -> Direct Contact via Email or Phone

revenueStreams.title: Revenue Streams
revenueStreams.instructions: Read each accounting document and assign it to the correct revenue stream category.

0.title: Document A: Monthly Access Fee
0.content: Invoice for recurring monthly access to the premium platform. Customer is billed automatically each month for continued service.

1.title: Document B: Product Purchase Receipt
1.content: Receipt for a single product purchase. The customer paid the full amount upfront with no recurring charges.

2.title: Document C: Metered Service Bill
2.content: Bill calculated based on actual usage this month: 150 API calls at $0.02 each. Total varies month to month depending on consumption.

3.title: Document D: Upgrade Invoice
3.content: Invoice for upgrading from the free tier to the Pro plan. The basic features remain free, but advanced features require payment.

feedback.wrong: That is not the right category. Re-read the document and consider how the payment works.
feedback.allCorrect: Excellent! You correctly classified all revenue stream documents!

revenueStreams.answerOverlay:
Correct classifications:
Document A (Monthly Access Fee) -> Subscription
Document B (Product Purchase Receipt) -> One-time Payment
Document C (Metered Service Bill) -> Usage-based Payment
Document D (Upgrade Invoice) -> Freemium

costStructure.title: Cost Structure
costStructure.instructions: Classify each monthly cost as either Fixed (stays the same regardless of output) or Variable (changes based on production/sales volume).

feedback.wrong: Some costs are incorrectly classified. The highlighted items need to be changed.
feedback.correct: Well done! You correctly classified all costs!

costStructure.answerOverlay:
Fixed costs: Office rent, Insurance, Loan payments, Employee salaries.
Variable costs: Sales commissions, Raw material, Packaging, Shipping.

canvas.title: Business Model Canvas
canvas.message: Congratulations! You have completed all five puzzles. Here is your completed Business Model Canvas. Hover over each block to learn more.

customerSegments.label: Customer Segments
customerSegments.description: The specific groups of people or organizations your business aims to serve. Good segments are specific, measurable, and actionable.

valueProposition.label: Value Proposition
valueProposition.description: The bundle of products and services that create value for a specific customer segment. It should clearly communicate the benefit without corporate jargon.

channels.label: Channels
channels.description: How your company communicates with and reaches its customer segments to deliver its value proposition.

revenueStreams.label: Revenue Streams
revenueStreams.description: The cash a company generates from each customer segment. Models include subscription, one-time, usage-based, and freemium.

costStructure.label: Cost Structure
costStructure.description: All costs incurred to operate a business model. Costs can be fixed (unchanged by volume) or variable (proportional to volume).

keyPartners.label: Key Partners
keyPartners.description: The network of suppliers and partners that make the business model work.

keyActivities.label: Key Activities
keyActivities.description: The most important things a company must do to make its business model work.

keyResources.label: Key Resources
keyResources.description: The most important assets required to make a business model work.

customerRelationships.label: Customer Relationships
customerRelationships.description: The types of relationships a company establishes with specific customer segments.

hints.explore: Look around the room. You can interact with the fogged window, the flip chart, the TV remote, the papers on the table, and the folder.
hints.window: Try clicking on the fogged window to start the Customer Segments puzzle.
hints.flipchart: The flip chart contains a value proposition exercise.
hints.tv: Use the TV remote to start the Channels puzzle.
hints.papers: The papers on the table contain accounting documents for the Revenue Streams puzzle.
hints.folder: The folder on the table has a monthly costs sheet for the Cost Structure puzzle.
hints.whiteboard: All puzzles are complete! Click the whiteboard to see your Business Model Canvas.
hints.default: Look around the room for interactive objects.
hints.puzzle_customers: Classify each customer profile as Valid or Invalid. Valid segments are specific and actionable; invalid ones are too broad, vague, or assumption-based.
hints.puzzle_channels: Use the arrows to scroll through the available channels and confirm the one that best matches the customer behavior shown.
hints.puzzle_revenue: Read each accounting document carefully, then drag it to the revenue stream category that best describes how the payment works.
hints.puzzle_costs: Assign each monthly cost to Fixed (same every month) or Variable (changes with production or sales volume), then check your answers.

completion.message: You have successfully completed the Business Planning escape room! You now understand the key components of a Business Model Canvas: Customer Segments, Value Proposition, Channels, Revenue Streams, and Cost Structure.
